newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Amnesty urges HK's future leader to uphold rights.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty urges HK's future leader to uphold rights.

text.p: Amnesty International on Wednesday urged Hong Kong's first post-colonial chief executive to uphold human rights after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule next year.
"Effective guarantees for human rights are not a luxury, but a basic requirement for Hong Kong," the London-based human rights group said in an open letter to shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa.
Hong Kong's Selection Committee, a Beijing-picked group of 400, named Tung as the territory's chief executive designate on Wednesday.
Tung will take office when China regains sovereignty over the colony on July 1, 1997, ending 150 years of British rule.
Hong Kong will become a Special Administrative Region of China.
Amnesty, which has been critical of human rights abuses in China, said it wished to discuss its concerns in Hong Kong with Tung at an early opportunity.
"No law passed by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region...should infringe upon or undermine...international human rights standards," Amnesty said.
"One pillar of Hong Kong's development is the effective protection and promotion of all human rights," Amnesty International Secretary General Pierre Sane said in the letter.
"In accordance with his earlier public statement, Tung Chee-hwa should ensure that the abolition of the death penalty in Hong Kong is not overturned," it said.
